\chapter{Exceptions}
\label{ch:ar-exceptions}
\hlchaptermodality{405}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk about an exception, and say that something excludes, includes, contains or concerns something.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 405: I can talk about an exception, and say that something excludes, includes, contains or concerns something.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استثناء} (istithnāʾ)}{استثناء (istithnāʾ)}]{\ar{استثناء} (istithnāʾ) — an exception}

\label{lesson:AR-C405-istithna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for as if, then the Arabic for to ensure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استثناء}}
\textbf{\ar{استثناء}} — \emph{istithnāʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}an exception\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لكل} \ar{قاعدة} \ar{استثناء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{li-kulli qāʿida istithnāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every rule has an exception.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استثناء}} (\emph{istithnāʾ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-n-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to fold, to bend back\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Istithnāʾ} is the Form X verbal noun, bending a thing back out of the rest: an exception.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istithnāʾ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istithnāʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-kulli qāʿida istithnāʾ.} — Every rule has an exception.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for as if, then the Arabic for to ensure, then say \emph{istithnāʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استثناء} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An exception\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استثنى} (istathnā)}{استثنى (istathnā)}]{\ar{استثنى} (istathnā) — to exclude}

\label{lesson:AR-C405-istathna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to ensure, then the Arabic for an exception.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استثنى}}
\textbf{\ar{استثنى}} — \emph{istathnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to exclude\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استثنى} \ar{المدير} \ar{الموظفين} \ar{الجدد} \ar{من} \ar{الاجتماع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istathnā al-mudīr al-muwaẓẓafīn al-judud min al-ijtimāʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager excluded the new employees from the meeting.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستثني}, \emph{yastathnī}.

It takes \ar{من}: \ar{استثنى} … \ar{من} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استثنى}} (\emph{istathnā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-n-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to fold, to bend back\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to bend a thing back out of a group: to exclude, to except.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istathnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istathnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istathnā al-mudīr al-muwaẓẓafīn al-judud min al-ijtimāʿ.} — The manager excluded the new employees from the meeting.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to ensure, then the Arabic for an exception, then say \emph{istathnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استثنى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To exclude\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شمل} (shamila)}{شمل (shamila)}]{\ar{شمل} (shamila) — to include}

\label{lesson:AR-C405-shamila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an exception, then the Arabic for to exclude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شمل}}
\textbf{\ar{شمل}} — \emph{shamila} — \textquotedblleft{}to include\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تشمل} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{زيارة} \ar{المتحف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tashmalu ar-riḥla ziyārat al-matḥaf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The trip includes a visit to the museum.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشمل}, \emph{yashmal}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شمل}} (\emph{shamila}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to comprise, to cover\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Shamila} is a Form I verb, to cover all of a thing: to include.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shamila}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shamila}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tashmalu ar-riḥla ziyārat al-matḥaf.} — The trip includes a visit to the museum.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an exception, then the Arabic for to exclude, then say \emph{shamila} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شمل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To include\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تضمن} (taḍammana)}{تضمن (taḍammana)}]{\ar{تضمن} (taḍammana) — to contain}

\label{lesson:AR-C405-tadammana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to exclude, then the Arabic for to include.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تضمن}}
\textbf{\ar{تضمن}} — \emph{taḍammana} — \textquotedblleft{}to contain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يتضمن} \ar{الكتاب} \ar{صورا} \ar{جميلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yataḍammanu al-kitāb ṣuwaran jamīla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The book contains beautiful pictures.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتضمن}, \emph{yataḍamman}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تضمن}} (\emph{taḍammana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be surety for\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to take a thing within oneself: to contain.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḍammana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḍammana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yataḍammanu al-kitāb ṣuwaran jamīla.} — The book contains beautiful pictures.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to exclude, then the Arabic for to include, then say \emph{taḍammana} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعلق} (taʿallaqa)}{تعلق (taʿallaqa)}]{\ar{تعلق} (taʿallaqa) — to concern}

\label{lesson:AR-C405-taallaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to include, then the Arabic for to contain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعلق}}
\textbf{\ar{تعلق}} — \emph{taʿallaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to concern\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يتعلق} \ar{الأمر} \ar{بصحة} \ar{أبي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yataʿallaqu al-amr bi-ṣiḥḥat abī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The matter concerns my father's health.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعلق}, \emph{yataʿallaq}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{يتعلق} \ar{بـ} …, it is about ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعلق}} (\emph{taʿallaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-l-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to hang, to cling\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to hang on a thing: to be attached to it, to concern it. \ar{علق}, to hang, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿallaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿallaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yataʿallaqu al-amr bi-ṣiḥḥat abī.} — The matter concerns my father's health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to include, then the Arabic for to contain, then say \emph{taʿallaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعلق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To concern\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 398–405 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R405-review-398-405}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for education and upbringing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item education, upbringing, a kindergarten, literacy, attendance
  \item unless, in case, provided that, as long as, otherwise
  \item if not for, whatever, whenever, whether, wherever
  \item a probability, probable, to tolerate, to consider likely, to rule out
  \item inevitably, necessarily, relatively, not at all, certainty
  \item to make certain, to be suspicious, impossible, most probably, in general
  \item a condition, to stipulate, even if, as if, to ensure
  \item an exception, to exclude, to include, to contain, to concern
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Education? (\textbf{\ar{تعليم}}, \emph{taʿlīm}.) Upbringing? (\textbf{\ar{تربية}}, \emph{tarbiya}.) A kindergarten? (\textbf{\ar{روضة}}, \emph{rawḍa}.) Literacy? (\textbf{\ar{محو} \ar{الأمية}}, \emph{maḥw al-ummiyya}.) Attendance? (\textbf{\ar{حضور}}, \emph{ḥuḍūr}.) Unless? (\textbf{\ar{إلا} \ar{إذا}}, \emph{illā idhā}.) In case? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{حال}}, \emph{fī ḥāl}.) Provided that? (\textbf{\ar{بشرط} \ar{أن}}, \emph{bi-sharṭi an}.) As long as? (\textbf{\ar{طالما}}, \emph{ṭālamā}.) Otherwise? (\textbf{\ar{وإلا}}, \emph{wa-illā}.) If not for? (\textbf{\ar{لولا}}, \emph{lawlā}.) Whatever? (\textbf{\ar{مهما}}, \emph{mahmā}.) Whenever? (\textbf{\ar{كلما}}, \emph{kullamā}.) Whether? (\textbf{\ar{سواء}}, \emph{sawāʾ}.) Wherever? (\textbf{\ar{أينما}}, \emph{aynamā}.) A probability? (\textbf{\ar{احتمال}}, \emph{iḥtimāl}.) Probable? (\textbf{\ar{محتمل}}, \emph{muḥtamal}.) To tolerate? (\textbf{\ar{احتمل}}, \emph{iḥtamala}.) To consider likely? (\textbf{\ar{رجح}}, \emph{rajjaḥa}.) To rule out? (\textbf{\ar{استبعد}}, \emph{istabʿada}.) Inevitably? (\textbf{\ar{حتما}}, \emph{ḥatman}.) Necessarily? (\textbf{\ar{بالضرورة}}, \emph{bi-ḍ-ḍarūra}.) Relatively? (\textbf{\ar{نسبيا}}, \emph{nisbiyyan}.) Not at all? (\textbf{\ar{إطلاقا}}, \emph{iṭlāqan}.) Certainty? (\textbf{\ar{يقين}}, \emph{yaqīn}.) To make certain? (\textbf{\ar{تيقن}}, \emph{tayaqqana}.) To be suspicious? (\textbf{\ar{ارتاب}}, \emph{irtāba}.) Impossible? (\textbf{\ar{مستحيل}}, \emph{mustaḥīl}.) Most probably? (\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الأرجح}}, \emph{ʿalā al-arjaḥ}.) In general? (\textbf{\ar{عموما}}, \emph{ʿumūman}.) A condition? (\textbf{\ar{شرط}}, \emph{sharṭ}.) To stipulate? (\textbf{\ar{اشترط}}, \emph{ishtaraṭa}.) Even if? (\textbf{\ar{حتى} \ar{لو}}, \emph{ḥattā law}.) As if? (\textbf{\ar{كما} \ar{لو}}, \emph{kamā law}.) To ensure? (\textbf{\ar{ضمن}}, \emph{ḍamina}.) An exception? (\textbf{\ar{استثناء}}, \emph{istithnāʾ}.) To exclude? (\textbf{\ar{استثنى}}, \emph{istathnā}.) To include? (\textbf{\ar{شمل}}, \emph{shamila}.) To contain? (\textbf{\ar{تضمن}}, \emph{taḍammana}.) To concern? (\textbf{\ar{تعلق}}, \emph{taʿallaqa}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
